Their IT-guy came over and spent just 10 minutes in

2101603687630266648.text:
Setting 1: Wi-Fi Channel Selection

Routers auto-select a wireless channel on setup day and then never touch it again — even as neighbors' routers pile onto that same channel over the following years.

In dense neighborhoods or apartment buildings, this creates constant

2101603775777784270.text:
Setting 2: 5GHz vs 2.4GHz Band Priority

Most devices default to connecting to whichever band they saw first — and once connected, they never automatically switch, even when a faster band is sitting right there unused.

The family's smart TV and laptop were both stuck on the

2101603846049214593.text:
Setting 3: QoS (Quality of Service)

Without QoS enabled, the router treats every device and every task with equal priority — meaning a phone downloading an app update can throttle a Zoom call happening at the exact same moment.

Most routers have this feature sitting disabled by

2101603917230747837.text:
Setting 4: Firmware Update

Routers almost never update themselves automatically, and most people have no idea firmware updates are even a thing that exists for their router.

An outdated firmware version means the router is missing years of speed improvements, security patches,

2101603981373894824.text:
Setting 5: DNS Server Change

Every device on the network uses whatever DNS server the ISP auto-assigns by default — and most ISP-provided DNS servers are slower and less reliable than free public alternatives.

DNS is what translates a website name into an actual connection, so

2101604052656361871.text:
Setting 6: Connected Devices Cleanup

Over years of use, routers accumulate dozens of "ghost" devices still technically connected or remembered — old phones, guests' laptops, devices that were sold or thrown away long ago.

Each of these can still be holding a reserved connection

Most iPhones get set up on day one and the Camera app is never touched again.

2101927156343529548.text:
Setting 1: Grid and Level
The iPhone camera defaults to a blank viewfinder. No guides. So almost every photo lands with the subject dead-center and the horizon a few degrees off. 

That is the single fastest way to make a good scene look like a tourist snap.

Go to Settings → https://t.co/gBvJ3Id0hh

2101927707319951411.text:

Tap the screen once and the phone keeps guessing. Move a step, and the face goes soft or the window blows out.

Tap and hold the thing you actually care about until a yellow banner says AE/AF LOCK.

Focus and exposure freeze. Then slide a finger up or down https://t.co/HnrwWvZ

2101928001185444158.text:
Setting 3: Photographic Styles

This is not a filter. A filter sits on top of a finished image. A Photographic Style changes how the camera processes colour and tone while the photo is being taken.

Apple ships it on Standard: safe, flat, inoffensive. Fine for everyone. Great for https://t.co/PQ3Xm8

2101928139035480223.text:

On a lot of recent iPhones the sensor can capture 24MP or 48MP. The camera still defaults lower to save storage.

That is the right default for WhatsApp. It is the wrong default if you crop, print, or zoom a reception photo later.

Go to Settings → Camera

2101928289426407476.text:

Go to Settings → Camera → Main Camera (some models say Fusion Camera).

Turn on the extra

2101928595648299132.text:

Tapping the on-screen shutter is how most blur happens. Your finger moves the phone at the exact moment it needs to be still.

Setting 1: Low Power Mode on battery only
macOS defaults to Automatic. Fine on paper. In practice the machine keeps doing background work while you’re unplugged and wondering why 80% became 40% before lunch.
Apple menu → System Settings → Battery
Set Low Power Mode to Only on

2102172622666805475.text:
Setting 2: Wake for network access
Your MacBook can wake itself from sleep to check mail, iCloud, and shared folders. Then it goes back to sleep. Then it wakes again.
That is how a lid-closed machine loses 20–30% overnight in a bag.
System Settings → Battery → Options
Wake for

2102172709614702948.text:
Setting 3: Power Nap off
Power Nap is Apple’s name for “keep doing work while you think this thing is asleep.” Mail. Time Machine. iCloud. Updates.
Useful on a desktop that sits on a desk. Less useful on a laptop that lives in a backpack.
System Settings → Battery → Options

2102172773594640568.text:
Setting 4: Login Items and background apps
Open the lid and 15 helpers wake up with you. Dropbox. Adobe. Teams. Spotify. A Google updater for a browser you used twice in 2024.
None of them ask. They just sit there.
System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions
Check both

2102172817882247302.text:

Settings can only catch what Apple labelled. The real drain is usually one app you left open.
Command + Space → type Activity Monitor → open it → click Energy
Sort by Energy Impact.
The top one or two rows are the story. Chrome with 40

2102172856910241923.text:

Pause for a day when you are out. Resume

Setting 7: Stop Spotlight indexing the whole disk

System Settings → Spotlight
Uncheck result categories you never search (fonts, web, Siri
